# NeuroGarval

**A CMS-driven, SEO-first static website for a small local business — built with plain HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript, generated by a single Python script, edited by a non-technical owner, deployed to GitHub Pages.**

Live site: [neurogarval.es](https://neurogarval.es)

This repository is the production site for NeuroGarval, a neuropsychology and health
psychology practice in Valdemoro (Madrid, Spain). It doubles as a **reference implementation**
for any small business, professional practice or local service that wants a fast, cheap,
fully-owned website which a non-programmer can update safely on their own.

## What this project is

A **single-page marketing website** for a psychology practice: hero, services,
care modalities (in-clinic / online / home visits), process, about the specialist,
blog, FAQ, contact section with an embedded map, and a footer with legal notice.
It is also a self-contained email signature template (`firma.html`).

Two things make it interesting as a reference project:

1. **The content lives in YAML, not in HTML.** An editor changes copy in a friendly
   web CMS (Pages CMS); a Python generator turns that YAML plus a small set of
   templates into the final static site.
2. **The build is the quality gate.** Every PR is generated and linted, and the
   site is only published from the protected `main` branch, so a bad edit can
   never reach production.

There is **no framework, no bundler, no `package.json`, no database and no server-side
code**. The published site is static HTML, one CSS file and one small JavaScript file.

## Why it exists

A solo professional practice needs a website that:

- can be updated **without a developer** and without breaking anything;
- is **fast and cheap** to host (free static hosting, no monthly maintenance);
- **ranks well in local search** and is easy for search engines and AI assistants
  to understand and quote;
- is **fully owned** — no proprietary builder that goes out of business or holds
  a hostage in five years;
- keeps **every piece of information consistent** (one phone number, one address,
  one set of SEO tags, everywhere).

The pipeline in this repository is the answer: content separated from presentation,
generation instead of editing, and Git as the review/audit trail.

## Feature overview

| Area | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Editing | Friendly web CMS ([Pages CMS](https://pagescms.org)) with one file per page section, Markdown support, image uploads, reusable components, Spanish labels, editor hints in field descriptions |
| Generation | One Python script resolves placeholders, expands loops, converts Markdown, generates structured data, writes contact data into the HTML, optimizes images and writes `_site/` |
| Sections | Hero, services, modalities, process, specialist, blog, FAQ, contact + embedded map, footer, email signature |
| Front-end | Semantic HTML5, one hand-written CSS file with design tokens, ~85 lines of vanilla JS that only opens modals and the mobile menu |
| Modals | Service / modality / blog detail modals built on the native `<dialog>` element, keyboard accessible |
| Images | Automatic PNG/JPEG → WebP conversion at build time, with `width`/`height`, `loading="lazy"` and `fetchpriority="high"` for the hero |
| SEO | Unique title/description/keywords, canonical URL, geo meta tags, Open Graph + Twitter cards, `sitemap.xml` with image entries, `robots.txt` |
| Structured data | Full JSON-LD graph generated by the build: `WebSite`, `MedicalBusiness` + `Psychologist`, `Person`, `hasOfferCatalog`, `FAQPage`, `BlogPosting` |
| AI/LLM | `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` generated from the same content, with a crawler-friendly `robots.txt` |
| Front matter | The domain lives in `src/CNAME`; every other fixed value (identity, language, locale, currency, SEO, social, menu labels, schema texts) lives in a read-only YAML file |
| Safety | Fail-fast build, four linters, required PR check, branch protection, scheduled smoke test of the live site |
| Publishing | Editor clicks "Publish changes" → PR `develop → main` → auto-merge when checks pass → automatic deploy |
| Cost | $0 hosting. GitHub Pages + GitHub Actions are free for public repositories; CMS and domains are the only costs |

## Architecture

### The content pipeline

```
        EDITOR (no code)                REPOSITORY                      CI / PUBLISHING
   ┌──────────────────────────┐   ┌───────────────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────────┐
   │  Pages CMS (develop)     │   │  content/*.yml   (data)   │   │  build.py                │
   │  - form fields           │──▶│  .pages.yml  (types)     │──▶│  - resolve markers       │
   │  - Markdown long text    │   │  src/*.html,*.txt,*.xml   │   │  - expand @foreach loops │
   │  - image uploads         │   │       (templates)         │   │  - Markdown → HTML       │
   │  - "Publish changes" btn │   │  media/       (assets)    │   │  - generate JSON-LD      │
   └──────────────────────────┘   │  src/CNAME   (domain)     │   │  - inject contact data   │
                                  │  scripts/build.py         │   │  - PNG/JPEG → WebP       │
                                  └───────────────────────────┘   │  - lint with prek        │
                                                                    │  - deploy to Pages       │
             ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
             ▼
      _site/  →  https://neurogarval.es  (static files only, no runtime)
```

### Markers: `__file.path.field__`

Templates contain placeholders whose first segment is the name of a content file:

```html
<title>__clinic_info.seo.title__</title>
<h1>__hero.title__ <i>__hero.title_accent__</i></h1>
<span class="badge">__hero.badge__</span>
```

`build.py` walks the YAML path, reads the field's **declared type** from `.pages.yml`
and renders it accordingly:

| Declared type | Rendered as |
| --- | --- |
| `rich-text` (Markdown) | converted to HTML with the `extra` extension |
| `image` | normalized `media/...` path plus a full `<img>` tag with dimensions and lazy loading |
| `component: icono` | inline SVG or a Bootstrap Icons class (single icon dictionary in `build.py`) |
| list of strings | joined (`, ` in the page, `·` in the hero modality line, new lines in `.txt` templates) |
| everything else | HTML-escaped plain text |

A few fields need more than their own value (the social image needs the site URL,
the sitemap needs absolute URLs, the hero modality line needs smart joining, the
whole JSON-LD graph is a special case). Those are handled by small **special
renderers** registered per template, exact route or glob pattern.

### Loops: repeated cards without copy-paste

Cards and list items are never written one by one. They are wrapped in a loop
block that the build repeats once per YAML element:

```html
<!-- @foreach:servicios.items -->
<div class="service-card" data-service="__servicios.items.n.id__"
     onclick="openServiceModal('__servicios.items.n.id__')">
    <h3>__servicios.items.n.title__</h3>
    <div class="markdown-content">__servicios.items.n.card_text__</div>
    <div class="card-full markdown-content" hidden>__servicios.items.n.modal_content__</div>
</div>
<!-- @endforeach:servicios.items -->
```

Inside the block, `n` means "the current element" and `__loop.index__` /
`__loop.index0__` give the 1-based / 0-based position (step numbers, modal indices).
**Adding or removing a service, modality, process step, blog post or FAQ question
in the CMS requires zero changes to the HTML** — including the modal wiring.

### `.pages.yml` doubles as the type registry

One file is both the CMS schema (collections, fields, components, media paths, the
"Publish changes" action) **and** the build's type registry. A field that is not
declared there does not exist as far as the generator is concerned, and the build
stops with a precise error. This makes the editor's form and the rendered markup
impossible to drift apart.

### One single source of truth for contact data

Phone, WhatsApp, email, address and the Maps link are edited once in
`content/common.yml`. The build then writes them **directly into the generated HTML**
(`tel:`, `wa.me`, `mailto:` and Maps links, plus the visible labels), so:

- the hero, contact section, footer and email signature can never disagree;
- nothing depends on JavaScript — the contact data is in the HTML a crawler receives;
- a change propagates to the JSON-LD and `llms.txt` automatically.

### Derived fields

A few values are computed instead of stored (`clinic_info.site.url`,
`common.contact.phone_tel`, `firma.web_label`, `firma.web_url`). The site URL is
derived from `src/CNAME`, so changing the domain is a one-line change.

### Fail-fast by design

The build aborts with an explicit message — naming the field, the template and the
reason — when a marker points to a missing file, a missing YAML path, an index out
of range, or a field that is not declared in `.pages.yml`. It also validates that
every service `id` exists and is unique before generating anything. A broken
template can never be deployed: the build *is* the test suite.

### Media pipeline: everything becomes WebP

Photos uploaded from the CMS arrive as PNG or JPEG. At build time they are converted
to WebP (quality 82) and **only** the WebP version is published, so the site always
serves light images without anyone converting files by hand. The single exception is
the `og:image`, which stays PNG because some social networks (WhatsApp, Facebook)
still refuse WebP.

## SEO and AI/LLM discoverability

Search and AI assistant visibility is treated as a feature of the build, not as an
afterthought:

- `<title>`, `description`, `keywords`, `canonical`, `geo.region` / `geo.placename` /
  `geo.icbm` from the content file;
- Open Graph and Twitter card tags, including image dimensions and alt text;
- a generated **JSON-LD graph**: `WebSite`, the practice as
  `["MedicalBusiness", "Psychologist"]` with address, geo coordinates parsed from the
  Maps embed, `areaServed` municipality list, `sameAs` social profiles and a
  `hasOfferCatalog`; the specialist as a `Person` with credential number; a
  `FAQPage` from the FAQ; a `BlogPosting` per post;
- `sitemap.xml` including the hero, specialist and blog images as `image:image` entries;
- `robots.txt` that explicitly allows all crawlers, including AI ones;
- **`llms.txt`** (a concise summary) and **`llms-full.txt`** (full text) — both
  generated from the same YAML, so they are never out of date;
- every long text already in the HTML (hidden `.card-full` blocks), so crawlers and
  LLM fetchers read the complete content without executing JavaScript.

## Repository layout

```
.
├── content/            # All editable content, one YAML file per page section
├── media/              # Images, favicon, logo, QR and PDFs (uploaded via the CMS)
├── src/                # Templates and static assets — never the finished page
│   ├── index.html      #   site template (markers + one JSON-LD marker)
│   ├── firma.html      #   standalone email signature template
│   ├── robots.txt      #   SEO/LLM templates, generated from the same content
│   ├── sitemap.xml
│   ├── llms.txt
│   ├── llms-full.txt
│   ├── styles.css      #   all CSS (design tokens, layout, responsive rules)
│   ├── script.js       #   modals + mobile menu only
│   └── CNAME           #   the domain (single source of truth)
├── scripts/
│   ├── build.py        # the generator (~1,180 lines, stdlib + PyYAML/Markdown/Pillow)
│   └── check_site.sh   # smoke test of the published site (curl only)
├── .pages.yml          # Pages CMS config + the build's type registry
├── .github/workflows/  # build validation, deploy, PR creation, live site check
├── .pre-commit/        # HTMLHint, Stylelint, ESLint and Lychee hooks
├── CONTRIBUTING.md     # short contributor guide (Spanish)
├── AGENTS.md           # detailed architecture/conventions for AI agents (Spanish)
└── _site/              # build output (gitignored, deleted and rebuilt every run)
```

## Content model

Each page section is a separate file, so the CMS form for a section is small and its
commits are reviewable in isolation.

| File | Section | CMS access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hero.yml` | Hero: badge, title, modality line, intro, promo, image | editable |
| `servicios.yml` | Services: cards + full modal copy, each with a stable `id` | editable |
| `modalidades.yml` | Care modalities: cards, modal copy, optional consultation photos | editable |
| `proceso.yml` | Process steps (icon, title, text) | editable |
| `especialista.yml` | About the specialist: photo, name, credential, bio | editable |
| `blog.yml` | Blog posts: cover, title, excerpt, full article | editable |
| `faq.yml` | FAQ questions and answers | editable |
| `contacto.yml` | Contact section: heading, highlight, Instagram, map embed | editable |
| `footer.yml` | Footer lines, legal notice link, copyright | read-only |
| `common.yml` | Phone, WhatsApp, email, address, Maps link (reused site-wide) | read-only |
| `clinic_info.yml` | Identity, language, locale, currency, logo, geo, SEO, social, menu labels, schema texts, service area, price range | read-only |
| `firma.yml` | Email signature copy | editable |

**Read-only means "not editable by the content editor"** — those files hold the fixed
identity of the business, so they are changed deliberately in a code review. The
editor can never accidentally break the canonical URL, the JSON-LD vocabulary or the
menu.

## Publishing workflow

```
editor clicks "Publish changes" in Pages CMS
        │
        ▼
create_pr.yml  (workflow_dispatch on develop)
        │   no changes vs main → nothing happens
        │   else → create (or reuse) PR develop → main, enable auto-merge (rebase)
        ▼
GitHub runs "Build Validation / build-validation" (required check on main)
        │   build.py + prek linters on the generated output
        ▼
merge lands on main
        │
        ▼
deploy_page.yml  (push to main) → build again → upload artifact → GitHub Pages
        │
        ▼
check_site.yml  (twice a day) verifies the published site still answers
```

Technical work follows the same path: changes are developed on `develop` and reach
`main` through the same reviewed PR. `main` is protected (PR required, status check
required) and is the only branch that deploys.

## Quality gates

| Gate | What it catches |
| --- | --- |
| `build.py` | Missing/misspelled content fields, undeclared types, duplicate service ids, missing static files |
| **HTMLHint** | Malformed tags, duplicated attributes, non-lowercase tag names, duplicate ids |
| **Stylelint** | CSS errors, unknown properties, bad syntax |
| **ESLint** | JavaScript problems |
| **Lychee** | Broken local and external links in the HTML (skips `tel:` links and template markers) |
| `check_site.sh` | Live site unreachable, empty, unresolved `__markers__`, missing `<title>`, missing canonical URL, no visible text, missing image, missing `robots.txt` / `sitemap.xml` / `llms*.txt` / logo / favicon |

`_site/` is gitignored, so CI stages it (`git add -f _site`) before running the
linters — the checks run against the **generated** site, not just the sources.

## Tech stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Front-end | Hand-written HTML5, CSS and vanilla JS | Zero dependencies, nothing to patch, works forever |
| Styling | One `styles.css` with CSS custom properties, Montserrat (Google Fonts) and Bootstrap Icons from CDN | No build step for CSS, design tokens in one place |
| Modals | Native `<dialog>` + `<details>` | Accessibility and behavior without a library |
| Content | YAML, one file per section | Human-readable, diff-friendly, framework-free |
| CMS | Pages CMS (`.pages.yml`) | Git-based, no vendor lock-in, free tier, per-field descriptions for the editor |
| Templating | Custom marker + `@foreach` engine in `build.py` | ~200 lines instead of a template engine dependency |
| Markdown | Python-Markdown (`extra`) | Editors write prose, the build renders HTML |
| Images | Pillow | WebP conversion at build time |
| Hosting | GitHub Pages | Free, HTTPS, versioned, globally cached |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions (4 workflows) | Free, required checks, auto-merge, scheduled checks |
| Hooks | `prek` (pre-commit compatible) with HTMLHint, Stylelint, ESLint, Lychee | Runs the same checks locally and in CI |
| Validation | Bash + `curl` | Live smoke test with no dependencies |

## Local development

Requirements: **Python 3.12** (the version CI uses), plus `pyyaml`, `markdown` and `pillow`.

```bash
# 1) Build the site into _site/
python -m pip install pyyaml markdown pillow
python scripts/build.py

# ... or without installing anything (uv):
uv run --with pyyaml --with markdown --with pillow python scripts/build.py
```

Then open **`_site/index.html`** in a browser. Never open `src/index.html` directly:
it still contains unresolved markers and empty contact slots.

```bash
# 2) Lint sources and the generated site
prek install --config .pre-commit/.pre-commit-config.yaml --force   # once
prek run --config .pre-commit/.pre-commit-config.yaml --all-files
git add -f _site   # prek only checks git-tracked files, and _site/ is gitignored

# 3) Check the published site (needs curl only)
bash scripts/check_site.sh
```

Manual QA checklist: every section anchor (`#inicio`, `#servicios`, `#modalidades`,
`#proceso`, `#especialista`, `#blog`, `#faq`, `#contacto`), one modal of each kind,
the mobile menu, and the contact links (phone, WhatsApp, email, Maps).

## Benefits

**For the business owner**

- Update prices, copy, services, photos, FAQ and blog posts from a browser, in minutes.
- Nothing to install, no hosting bill, no plugin updates, no maintenance windows.
- The website keeps working even if every third-party service disappears tomorrow.
- A clear audit trail: who changed what, when, and the change passed the build.

**For a developer or maintainer**

- No framework to upgrade, no lockfile drift, no supply-chain surface.
- Content changes and structural changes are separated: most PRs touch one YAML file.
- The build is deterministic and self-validating — it either produces a complete site or fails loudly.
- About 2,600 lines of hand-written code in total: ~1,400 for the site itself
  (template, CSS, JS) and ~1,200 for the generator.
- Easy to fork: same pattern works for a restaurant, a law firm, a dental clinic or a portfolio.

**For visitors and search engines**

- Static HTML: fast first paint, no client-side rendering, no layout shift.
- Readable with JavaScript disabled; accessible with keyboard and screen readers.
- Rich structured data, local SEO signals, and explicit text for AI assistants.
- Light pages: one CSS file, one small script, WebP images, no trackers or cookie banner.

## Reusing this for another business

The repository is deliberately generic. A fork typically needs:

1. **Rename the domain**: edit `src/CNAME`. The site URL, canonical tag, sitemap,
   `llms.txt` links and the signature URL are all derived from it.
2. **Rewrite the identity**: `content/clinic_info.yml` (name, language, locale,
   currency, logo, locality, geo coordinates, SEO and social tags, menu labels,
   schema texts, `areaServed`, price range).
3. **Rewrite the content**: one file per section in `content/`. Add or remove whole
   sections by editing `src/index.html` and the section's YAML together; keep the
   `@foreach` blocks intact.
4. **Replace the assets**: `media/` — logo, favicon, hero and section images, legal PDFs.
   The `og:image` must stay a PNG (`image.png`).
5. **Adjust the schema types if needed**: the generator builds
   `["MedicalBusiness", "Psychologist"]` for a clinic. For another sector, change the
   type list and the fields it reads in `jsonld_graph()` in `build.py`; the vocabulary
   stays in the YAML as much as possible.
6. **Extend the icon dictionary** if you need icons that do not exist: add an inline SVG
   or Bootstrap Icons class to `ICONS` in `build.py` and the same value to the
   `icono` component options in `.pages.yml`.
7. **Rebuild and review**: `python scripts/build.py`, open `_site/index.html`, run the linters.
8. **Set up hosting once**: in the fork's *Settings → Pages*, set the source to
   "GitHub Actions"; enable auto-merge with rebase; protect `main` with a required PR
   and the `Build Validation / build-validation` check. Update the check name in
   `create_pr.yml` if you rename the workflow.

You do **not** need to touch the content model, the marker system, the loops, the
build, the linters or the workflows for most changes.

## Design principles and conventions

- **Content and presentation are separated.** Templates hold structure; YAML holds
  values; the build joins them.
- **Every site-specific literal is in content, not in code.** The domain comes from
  `src/CNAME`; identity, SEO, social tags, menu labels and structured-data texts come
  from `clinic_info.yml`. Code contains only markup, classes, icon names and
  schema.org vocabulary.
- **One source of truth per fact.** Contact details, keywords, service catalogue,
  FAQ, posts — each lives in exactly one place and is reused everywhere.
- **Fail fast, never silently.** Unresolved content is a build error, not a broken page.
- **Progressive enhancement.** Full content is in the HTML; JavaScript only enhances it.
- **No hardcoded copies of lists.** Loops, not repeated markup.
- **Content files stay machine-clean.** Exactly the format the CMS writes: no YAML
  comments, no blank lines between fields. Editor guidance lives in the `description`
  of each field in `.pages.yml`.
- **Do not introduce a framework or bundler.** That is the whole point of the project.

## Current limitations / ideas

- Blog posts open in a modal; there are no standalone article pages yet (a `content/posts/`
  collection is already sketched at the end of `.pages.yml`).
- Single-language content. The marker system is language-agnostic, so a second locale
  would mean duplicate content files plus `hreflang` handling.
- No analytics and no contact form (the practice is contacted by phone, WhatsApp or email).
- `build.py` is a single file; splitting it into modules is a pending refactor that must
  keep the generated output byte-identical.
